title: Intent-aware access auditor, role-based retention, and prompt scrubbing
creator: Carmen Liu
description: We need an intent-aware access auditor service that ties RBAC decisions to differential retention policies. The goal is to prevent overexposure of PII and prompt content in trace/log pipelines by evaluating access intent (debugging vs incident review vs analytics) and applying dynamic scrubbing and retention caps. This ticket implements the backend pipeline, integration hooks for tracing libraries, access-policy mapping, and console UX for per-request audit replay requests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Requests with 'debug' intent and role=platform_engineer should retain full trace for 7 days and have immutable access logs. 2) Requests with 'analytics' intent and role=analyst should have prompt content removed and traces trimmed to 2 hops; retention 30 days. 3) All access actions are logged in immutable audit entries including request_id, viewer_role, intent_tag and scrub_rules_applied. 4) Console exposes 'request reveal' workflow where authorized reviewers can request temporary unmasking; approvals are recorded and TTL enforced. 5) Integration tests simulate role/intents and validate scrubbers and retention enforcement end-to-end.
implementation_notes: Architecture: new 'intent-auditor' microservice subscribes to observability-ingest kafka topic and attaches access metadata to event headers. Tracing hooks will emit an intent tag derived from SDK flags and endpoint parameters. The auditor will consult PolicyStore (policy ids referenced in labels) to determine scrub pipeline (field masks, prompt redaction regexes, pseudonymization salt) and retention TTL. We'll add policy evaluation caching (TTL 5m) and deny-by-default for missing policies. Use existing scrubbers library with a new 'prompt-aware' plugin that uses model-specific tokens to avoid over-redaction. Store audit entries in access-audit-sstable with HMACed viewer identifier. Fallback behavior: if PolicyStore unreachable, default to conservative scrubbing and emit incident metric.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation, integration tests using synthetic traces with embedded prompt-like fields, e2e test with local kafka, verification of audit log immutability, load test to ensure auditor can handle peak ingest. Add mutation tests for scrub regex to avoid accidental PII leakage. Add staged rollout with canary traffic and metric guardrails (error rate, added latency, scrub-failure rate).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag enable auditor in dev and staging; 2) Canary on 1% of production ingest for 48hrs with heavy monitoring; 3) Scale to 20% for 24hrs; 4) Full rollout with 72hr observation window. Provide rollback toggle and 'conservative-scrub' emergency mode. Communicate to security and SRE teams pre-rollout.
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: increased ingest latency (target <5ms per event). Mitigation: async processing with immediate-enqueue path and token-based sampling for synchronous critical traces. Risk: false positives in prompt scrubbing removing semantic content. Mitigation: have 'reveal request' workflow and test harness for regex tuning. Risk: audit log tampering. Mitigation: append-only storage with signed entries and retention policy.
open_questions: How to derive intent reliably from SDKs when callers don't provide explicit flags?
What is the HSM strategy for signing audit entries?
Should 'alerting' intent allow longer retention by default?
